beats.text: Batch: wait for midnight. Some answers can't wait.
beats.say: Batch processing waits until the end of the day, then crunches all the data at once. But some answers can't wait.

beats.text: Stream: handle each event as it arrives.
beats.say: Stream processing handles each event as it arrives, continuously, in near real time.
To count things over time, it groups events into windows, like the number of clicks per minute.

beats.text: Late events: event time and watermarks.
beats.say: Events can arrive late or out of order. So the processor tracks event time, and uses watermarks to decide when a window is complete.

beats.text: State + checkpoints: no loss, no double counting.
beats.say: It also keeps state, like running counts, and checkpoints it, so after a crash it resumes without losing or double counting events.
Popular tools include Kafka Streams, Flink, and Spark Streaming.
